In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat ash-Shams

It is Meccan.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the sun and its brightness﴾. That is: its light. It is also said: it is the entire day.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 91, verse 2:

And His saying: ﴿And the moon when it follows it﴾, meaning: it follows it (tabi'aha). This is the view of Mujahid, Qatadah and the majority of the exegetes, and it is also related from Ibn 'Abbas. The meaning of "it follows it" is that when the sun sets, the moon follows it in light. It is said: it refers to the white days, when the sun sets and the moon rises. It is also said: it refers to the first night of the month, when the sun sets and the crescent (hilal) is sighted. In general, the moon is one of the two luminaries, and it follows the sun when it becomes full and completes its illumination of the world.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 91, verse 3:

And as for His saying: ﴿By the day when it reveals it﴾, there are two opinions. The first: it reveals the darkness, so the darkness is referred to by implication without being mentioned, and this is common in the speech of the Arabs. The second opinion: "it reveals it" means it reveals the sun, because when the day rises, the sun shines and spreads out.
And His saying: ﴿By the night when it covers it﴾ means: when it covers the sun, that is, conceals its light.

and His saying: ﴿By the heaven and He who built it﴾ — its meaning is: "and He who built it." It is also said: "and the One who built it."

It is narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr that he heard the sound of thunder and said: "Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies" — that is, "Glory be to the One whom it glorifies." It is also said: "wa-ma banaha" means "and its building" (wa-binaihā).
And His saying: ﴿By the earth and He who spread it out﴾. That is, by He who spread it out. It is also said: "the earth and its spreading out" (ṭaḥwuhā), meaning its extension.

And His saying: ﴿And a soul and He who proportioned it﴾. That is: and He who proportioned it. We have already explained the meaning of "tasmiyah" (naming). It has also been said: it refers to the uprightness of the stature.

And His saying: ﴿So He inspired it with its wickedness and its God-consciousness﴾. That is: He made it know and informed it (of them). Mujahid, al-Dahhak and others said: He placed within its heart its wickedness and its God-consciousness. And this is preferable to the first statement, because inspiration (al-ilham) in the language is above mere making-known and informing.

And al-Zajjaj said: He made it balanced (ʿaddalahā) for wickedness, and enabled it (wafaqahā) for God-consciousness.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 91, verse 9:

﴿Indeed, he has succeeded who purifies it.﴾ On this basis the oath is completed, and the meaning is: Indeed, the soul has succeeded that Allah has purified.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 91, verse 10:

And His saying: ﴿And he has indeed failed who covers it [with corruption]﴾. That is: and the soul has failed that Allah covered (dassahā). It was also said: the one who purifies his soul and sets it right has succeeded, and the one who extinguishes his soul and buries it has failed. According to this, His saying ﴿dassāhā﴾ means dassīhā (he buried it).

The poet says:

(Yaqḍī al-bāzī idhā al-bāzī inkasar...)

That is: yaqaḍḍu al-bāzī (the falcon breaks, i.e. tears apart, the falcon).

Al-Farrā' said: the one who acts in immorality is obscure among people, of hidden person, bowed head, while the one who is God-fearing is elevated and high.

Thaʿlab said: "man dassāhā" means he led it astray (aghwāhā). And it is related from him that he said: dassāhā means he thrust himself (dassa nafsahu) among the people of good while he was not one of them.

The poet says:

(Wa-anta alladhī dassayta ʿAmran fa-aṣbaḥat / ḥalāʾiluhu minhu arāmila ḍaʿā)

And His saying "dassāhā" here means: destroyed it. According to this, the meaning of His saying ﴿And he has indeed failed who covers it﴾ is: he destroyed it through sins.

Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUmar al-Jumaḥī narrated, from Ibn Abī Mulaykah, who said: ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: I woke up one night and found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "O Allah, grant my soul its piety, and purify it, for You are the best to purify it. You are its Guardian and its Master."

He (may Allah have mercy on him) said: This was related to us by Abū al-Ghanāʾim ʿAbd al-Ṣamad ibn ʿAlī al-ʿAbbāsī, who said: Abū al-Qāsim ʿĪsā ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā informed us, who said: al-Baghawī informed us, who said: Dāwūd ibn ʿAmr al-Ḍabbī informed us, from Nāfiʿ ibn ʿUmar... the hadith.
"And His saying: ﴿Thamud denied [their prophet] in their transgression﴾ — that is, in their rebellion (bi-taghyanihā). It is also said: with all of them (bi-ajma'iha)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 91, verse 12:

And His words: ﴿When the most wretched of them was sent forth﴾ refers to Qudar ibn Salif, and We have explained this earlier.

Rushdin related, from Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn Salama, from Uthman ibn Suhayb, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Ali: "Who is the most wretched of the first (people)?" He said: "The one who hamstrung the she-camel." He said: "You have spoken the truth." He said: "Then who is the most wretched of the last (people)?" He said: "I said: I do not know, O Messenger of Allah."

He said: "The one who will strike you on this," and he gestured with his hand toward his crown (yafukh, the top of the head).

He, may Allah be pleased with him, said: This was reported to us by Karima bint Ahmad, who said: Abu Ali Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us, Muhammad ibn Idris [al-Sami] informed us, Suwayd ibn Sa'id informed us, from Rushdin... the report, and it is gharib (rare, a report transmitted through a weak or single channel).

And His saying: ﴿Then the Messenger of Allah said to them﴾, and he is Salih.

And His saying: ﴿the she-camel of Allah and her drink﴾. That is: leave the she-camel of Allah and her drink. The meaning of "her drink" is her turn to drink, as He said elsewhere: ﴿She shall have a drink, and you shall have a drink, on a known day﴾.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 91, verse 14:**

And His saying: ﴿So they denied him and hamstrung her﴾, meaning: they denied Salih, and hamstrung the she-camel.

And His saying: ﴿So their Lord crushed them over their sin﴾. It is related from Ibn al-Zubayr that he read it as "fa-ramrama 'alayhim rabbuhum" (ﻓﺮﻣﺮﻡ), and this is the meaning of the well-known recitation. It is also said: "dammama" means that their Lord became angry with them; one says "fulan yudamdimu" when he speaks in anger.

The well-known view is that the meaning of His saying ﴿He crushed them﴾ is: He closed over them with the punishment, meaning He encompassed them and left none of them alive. It is also said that al-damdama is destruction by uprooting.

And His saying: ﴿over their sin, and levelled them﴾, meaning: He levelled them with the ground, so that none of them was left, young or old.

It is also said: He made them all equal in the punishment.

"And His words: ﴿and He does not fear its consequence﴾. It is also recited as "فَلَا يخَاف عقباها" (fa-la yakhāfu ʿuqbāhā). In this there are two opinions. The first: that God, exalted is He, does not fear that anyone will pursue Him for what He has done; this was said by al-Ḥasan and others. The second opinion: the one who hamstrung the she-camel did not fear the consequence of his action. And God knows best."
